name: Ironbloom Crews (The Wall Dialect)
description: Ironbloom is the dominant graffiti tradition of the Gray Zone, distinguished by its use of bioluminescent pigments, chrome-reactive spray compounds, and layered stencil-over-freehand technique that creates images visible differently under natural light, UV, and BCI-overlay scanning. The aesthetic is dense and accumulative — no blank surface survives long in Ironbloom territory — and pieces are deliberately built over each other in dialogue rather than competition, creating palimpsests called Walls. Three major crews define the scene: KESSRA (geometric abstraction), the Moth Collective (figurative, memorial-focused), and SILT (text-heavy, political, most surveilled). Turf is marked not by territory but by stylistic dominance — a KESSRA piece incorporating Moth Collective elements signals respect or alliance.
cultural_impact: Ironbloom Walls have become de facto public records in the Gray Zone neighborhoods — memorials for the dead, warnings about unsafe buildings, and coded maps of ghost market locations. Halversen-Okeke's cultural appropriation division has twice attempted to license Ironbloom aesthetics for commercial use, both times resulting in the targeted defacement of their Tier 3 properties within 72 hours.
key_figures: Reina Osaghae-Kowalczyk (KESSRA founder, now semi-retired, teaches workshops)
The Moth Collective (anonymous rotating membership, no individual named publicly)
Dav Subramaniam-Osei (SILT's most wanted writer, Φ 8,000 corporate bounty active)
locations: The Foundry Wall, the Gray Zone Sector 11 (oldest continuous Ironbloom surface, 34 years of layers)
Condemned Block 7, Northwest the Gray Zone (primary SILT territory)
The Underpass Cathedral, Sector 4 (Moth Collective memorial space)
story_hooks: A SILT piece that appeared overnight encodes something more than political sloganeering — read through a BCI overlay, it contains a map to something that should not exist.
The Foundry Wall is slated for demolition to make way for a Tier 2 upzoning project; the three major crews must decide whether to unite in opposition or scatter before the corporate security sweep.

Someone is commissioning high-quality forgeries of Moth Collective memorial pieces — placing them in locations where no one died — and the Collective wants to know who is desecrating their language and why.
